Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the MedTech Innovations Inc. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO; Jennifer Lee, CFO; Dr. Michael Chen, Chief Technology Officer; and David Patel, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Alex Rivera.

Dr. Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. MedTech Innovations achieved record results this quarter, reflecting the strength of our diversified portfolio and our commitment to innovation.

Today, I will cover eight key aspects of our performance. First, the impact of our pricing and cost management initiatives. Second, our R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress. Third, gross margin trends and supply chain commentary. Fourth, new product launches and their contribution to growth. Fifth, hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates. Sixth, capital equipment versus consumables mix trends. Seventh, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains. And eighth, procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary.

Jennifer will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Michael will update us on our technology advancements, and David will discuss our market strategies. We'll then conclude with a Q&A session.

Now, let's get started with the impact of our pricing and cost management initiatives. These efforts were key drivers behind our beat on both top- and bottom-line results this quarter. They delivered approximately $225 million in incremental profitability year-over-year, contributing to a 320 basis point expansion in adjusted gross margins to 68.2%—our highest level in over five years—and helping us achieve 12% core organic revenue growth excluding foreign exchange headwinds.

Starting with pricing initiatives, we realized a robust 3.2% average selling price uplift across our portfolio. This marks the third consecutive quarter of sequential ASP gains, up from 2.8% in Q2, and reflects disciplined execution in a dynamic reimbursement landscape. In our Cardiovascular franchise—our largest segment at 42% of revenues—we captured a 4.1% ASP increase on our next-gen drug-eluting stents, similar to the premium pricing dynamics we've seen from peers like Boston Scientific with their Synergy platform. This was bolstered by favorable U.S. CMS final rules for FY2025, which preserved pass-through status for our SynthoStent platform, adding roughly 150 basis points to our U.S. pricing power.

Regionally, the U.S. drove 65% of our pricing tailwind, with ASPs up 4.5% amid strong hospital demand for high-acuity procedures and our shift toward value-based contracts. In Europe, we navigated pricing pressures from HTA bodies like NICE in the UK and IQWiG in Germany by emphasizing clinical differentiation—our OrthoFlex hip implants, for instance, secured 2.8% ASP growth through superior 5-year revision rates of under 1.5%, outperforming the category average. Emerging markets, particularly China and India, presented a more volume-leveraged story: while ASPs were flat to slightly down 0.5% due to National Reimbursement Drug List negotiations, we offset this with 18% procedure volume growth in structural heart devices, mirroring trends at Abbott's Amplatzer portfolio.

Strategically, we're accelerating our transition to bundled pricing models, with 28% of U.S. contracts now tied to outcomes-based rebates—think reduced readmissions for our neuromodulation leads, akin to Medtronic's Intellis platform. This not only supports premium pricing but positions us for the shift to site-neutral payments under the Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act extensions.

Shifting to cost management, our initiatives generated $180 million in run-rate savings this quarter, on track for our $750 million full-year target. Supply chain optimization was the standout, accounting for 55% of savings. We've consolidated our supplier base by 22% since Q1 2023, locking in multi-year agreements with strategic partners like DuPont for high-performance polymers used in our da Vinci-inspired robotic catheters. This mitigated 7% inflation in resin costs, which spiked post-Ukraine supply disruptions.

In manufacturing, we've rolled out Industry 4.0 digital twins across our Galway, Ireland, and Tijuana facilities, yielding a 14% reduction in cycle times for pacemaker assembly—directly comparable to Intuitive Surgical's efficiency gains on da Vinci Xi production. Automation investments, including AI-driven defect detection, drove 9% lower scrap rates, expanding factory utilization to 88% from 82% a year ago. Raw material hedging covered 75% of our 2024 exposure, shielding us from titanium price volatility, which remains elevated at $28 per kg versus $22 pre-pandemic.

On the operating side, SG&A leverage improved to 24.1% of revenues through zero-based budgeting and a 6% headcount optimization in non-core functions, while R&D productivity rose with a 15% faster time-to-clinic for our pipeline assets via virtual modeling—saving $45 million annually without compromising our 11% R&D intensity.

Looking holistically, these initiatives have de-risked our P&L amid macro headwinds: input costs are now running 2% below plan, and we're entering 2025 with enhanced pricing visibility from 85% of contracts renewed at higher rates. This resilience mirrors the playbook of Stryker and Zimmer Biomet, who similarly expanded margins through ortho mix shift and lean initiatives during the post-COVID recovery. In summary, pricing and cost management aren't just tactical—they're foundational to our 15-17% medium-term EBITDA margin algorithm. We're confident this momentum sustains our 8-10% organic growth outlook, even as we invest $1.2 billion in next-gen innovations like bioresorbable scaffolds.

Now, let's talk about our R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress. As a cornerstone of our long-term growth strategy in the $500 billion-plus global medical devices market, we're navigating a dynamic landscape shaped by aging demographics, the shift toward value-based care, and accelerating demand for minimally invasive and digital-enabled solutions. Our focus remains on high-margin, differentiated products that address unmet needs in structural heart, neuromodulation, orthopedics, and digital diagnostics.

In Q3, we invested $178 million in R&D, representing 11.8% of our quarterly revenue—up 12% year-over-year and ahead of our peer group average of around 10%, as reported in recent filings from Medtronic and Boston Scientific. For the full year, we're on track to hit $720 million in R&D spend, or 12.5% of projected revenues, reflecting our commitment to outpacing industry growth rates. This is up from 10.2% in FY2023, driven by a 25% ramp-up in clinical trial expenses and a strategic 18% increase in headcount for our engineering and data science teams, now totaling over 1,200 globally. These investments are already yielding a strong ROI: our R&D-to-new-product-revenue ratio stands at 1.8x over the past 24 months, with innovations contributing 28% of our top-line growth last year.

Turning to pipeline progress, we made significant milestones across all stages. In our structural heart franchise—our largest at 35% of revenues—we advanced our next-gen transcatheter aortic valve replacement platform, the ApexFlow Ultra, into pivotal trials. Building on the success of our first-gen ApexFlow, which captured 15% U.S. market share in intermediate-risk patients within 18 months of launch, the Ultra features a repositionable, low-profile design with bioresorbable components to reduce paravalvular leak rates by an anticipated 40%. Enrollment is complete in our 800-patient U.S. and EU randomized controlled trial, with topline data expected Q2 2025 and FDA submission targeted for H2. Early safety data shows a 98% procedural success rate, positioning us to challenge Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien franchise head-on.

In neuromodulation, where we're targeting the $8 billion spinal cord stimulation market growing at 12% CAGR, our ReNeuve AI platform hit a key inflection point. This closed-loop system uses machine learning algorithms to dynamically adjust stimulation parameters based on real-time patient pain biomarkers, potentially improving responder rates from the current 60-70% industry benchmark to over 85%. We've completed IDE approval for a 500-patient U.S. trial and secured CE Mark in Europe, with first implants underway in Germany and the Nordics. Partnerships with NVIDIA for edge AI processing and Mayo Clinic for biomarker validation have accelerated development by six months.

Orthopedics remains a bright spot amid supply chain headwinds. Our Trinity Porous Acetabular System, leveraging 3D-printed tantalum scaffolds for enhanced osseointegration, received FDA 510(k) clearance last month—our third ortho approval this year. Initial U.S. launch data shows 25% faster stem-to-cage integration versus Stryker's Tritanium, and we're scaling manufacturing at our Limerick, Ireland facility to support 50,000 units annually by FY2026. Regionally, this positions us strongly in Asia-Pacific, where we've filed for NMPA approval in China through our JV with Shanghai MicroPort, tapping into a market projected to grow 15% amid rising hip/knee replacements.

On the digital health front, our CardioLink wearable ECG monitor—integrated with our cloud-based AI platform—progressed to late-stage validation. This device targets atrial fibrillation detection in high-risk populations, boasting 96% sensitivity in our 10,000-patient real-world study, rivaling Apple Watch metrics but with FDA-cleared clinical-grade accuracy. We've expanded pilots with Kaiser Permanente in the U.S. and the NHS in the UK, generating $12 million in early access revenue this quarter.

Strategically, we're prioritizing three pillars: precision tech integration, with 40% of our pipeline now incorporating AI/ML or robotics, up from 22% in 2022; sustainability, via recyclable biomaterials in 60% of new devices to meet EU MDR and California's SB1383 mandates; and emerging markets expansion, where 25% of R&D budget now funds localization efforts like our INRIDE program for low-cost insulin delivery devices in India and Brazil. Risks include clinical trial delays—we've built in 15% contingency—and regulatory scrutiny, but our 92% Phase II-to-approval success rate over five years gives us confidence.

Looking ahead, we expect our pipeline to drive $450 million in incremental revenue by FY2027, with 7-9 new product launches, including two potential blockbusters in heart failure and robotics-assisted endoscopy. This positions us to grow EPS at 14-16% CAGR through the decade, outpacing the industry's 8-10%.

Moving on to gross margin trends and supply chain commentary. We delivered a strong quarter with GAAP gross margin of 68.2%, up 210 basis points year-over-year and 50 basis points sequentially from Q2. On a non-GAAP basis, excluding certain amortization and restructuring charges, our gross margin expanded to 69.5%, representing our 10th consecutive quarter of year-over-year improvement. This brings our trailing 12-month non-GAAP gross margin to 68.9%, positioning us at the high end of our med device peer set—think along the lines of Edwards Lifesciences in structural heart or Intuitive Surgical in robotics—while we continue to scale our portfolio across our core franchises in cardiovascular interventions, orthopedics, and neuromodulation.

Key drivers included a favorable product mix shift of approximately +140 basis points. Our higher-margin structural heart portfolio, led by our next-gen TAVR platform—the NovaFlow Transcatheter Valve, which we launched in Europe last year—grew 28% year-over-year and now represents 22% of total revenue, up from 17% a year ago. This premium segment, with ASPs averaging $28,000 per procedure kit, significantly outpaces our legacy coronary stent business, where margins are closer to 62%. Similarly, in orthopedics, our robotic-assisted knee implant system, NovaKnee AI, saw U.S. procedure volumes up 35%, driven by our expanded indications for outpatient ASCs. This mix benefit was partially offset by softer demand in our commodity-like electrophysiology catheters amid payer pushback on reimbursement in the U.S., but overall, it's a testament to our strategy of prioritizing innovation-led growth over volume in low-margin segments.

Manufacturing productivity and cost discipline added +110 basis points. We realized $24 million in sequential COGS savings, primarily from yield improvements in our Singapore cleanroom facilities, where we've ramped automation on our neuromodulation leads—think deep brain stimulation devices akin to Medtronic's Activa line. Our factory utilization hit 88% globally, up from 82% last year, thanks to our Enterprise Cost Transformation program, which includes AI-optimized CNC machining for titanium implants and lean Six Sigma initiatives reducing scrap rates by 15% in orthopedics. Raw material costs, particularly medical-grade PEEK polymers and cobalt-chrome alloys, were managed through forward contracts locked in at Q1 2023 pricing, shielding us from the 8-10% inflation seen industry-wide per the PPI data.

Pricing actions contributed +40 basis points. We implemented modest 2-3% list price increases on our U.S. durable equipment like our neuromodulation IPGs, with net pricing holding steady at 101% of list after routine contracting. In Europe, where we've faced headwinds from the MDR transition—similar to what Boston Scientific has navigated with their Watchman LAAO device—we secured favorable reimbursement for NovaFlow in Germany and France, adding 1.5 points to realized pricing.

Offsetting these were foreign exchange as a 30 basis point drag, driven by the strengthening USD against the Euro and Yen, impacting our 45% international revenue mix. Freight and logistics costs rose modestly due to Red Sea disruptions, adding $4 million to COGS, though this was only 20 bps after mitigation. And inventory provisions ticked up $2 million for excess slow-moving peripheral vascular stents, reflecting a deliberate portfolio pruning.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 non-GAAP gross margin to land in the 69.5% to 70.5% range, with further mix expansion from our U.S. TAVR launch in H1 2025 and productivity gains offsetting any seasonal FX volatility. Over the medium term, our target remains 72%+ by FY2026, aligning with peers like Abbott in diabetes care as we derisk our cost base.

Shifting to supply chain commentary, which has been a differentiator for us amid the sector's ongoing challenges. Medical devices rely on a complex, just-in-time ecosystem involving specialized actives like platinum-iridium coils for neurovascular stents, biologics for tissue-engineered heart valves, and semiconductors for our imaging-guided cath lab systems. Post-COVID, we've seen persistent bottlenecks: the 2023 ballooning of lead times for ethylene oxide sterilization capacity, now at 18-24 weeks industry-wide per ISPE benchmarks, or the titanium supply crunch from geopolitical tensions in Ukraine and China.

That said, our supply chain resilience score—tracked internally via our SCOR model—stands at 92/100, up from 84 a year ago, thanks to three pillars: supplier diversification and nearshoring, accounting for 60% of impact. We've reduced single-source dependency from 28% to 12% of critical components. For instance, our cobalt-chrome powder for orthopedic implants, previously 80% from a single Chinese supplier, is now dual-sourced with a new U.S. facility from Carpenter Technology, cutting lead times by 40%. We've also nearshored 25% of our electronics assembly to our greenfield plant in Tijuana, Mexico—mirroring Stryker's moves—which serves our U.S. West Coast distribution and mitigates tariff risks under USMCA. In Asia, we're ramping a second supplier in Vietnam for catheter extrusions, hedging against U.S.-China trade frictions that have hit peers like BD in their vascular access lines.

Vertical integration and digital twins account for 25% of impact. We're insourcing balloon catheter manufacturing, previously 100% outsourced, with our new Galway, Ireland facility coming online in Q1 2025. This will capture 300 bps of margin uplift long-term. We've deployed digital twin technology—using Siemens NX software—to simulate supply disruptions, allowing us to pre-build 14 weeks of safety stock on high-velocity SKUs like our coronary drug-eluting stents without tying up excess working capital. Our inventory turns improved to 4.8x from 4.2x YoY, balancing resilience with efficiency.

Regional agility and risk mitigation make up 15% of impact. U.S. operations remain rock-solid, with no disruptions from FDA's increased scrutiny on sterile packaging. In Europe, MDR compliance has delayed some supplier quals, but we've accelerated ISO 13485 audits for our Italian partners on structural heart components. China volumes grew 15% but we're capping exposure at 18% of supply base via our "China+1" policy. Emerging markets like India and LATAM are bright spots, with local-for-local production of orthopedic trauma plates starting in Brazil next quarter.

We've stress-tested for scenarios like another EO shortage or rare earth magnet constraints for our LVADs, maintaining 98% on-time delivery to hospitals. Capex for supply chain initiatives was $45 million this quarter, within our $220 million full-year guide, funding robotics like ABB arms in our Galway line for 20% labor productivity gains.

In summary, our gross margin trajectory reflects disciplined execution amid a favorable industry backdrop—global med device growth at 5-7% per Evaluate MedTech, fueled by aging demographics and procedure backlogs. Supply chain-wise, we're not just surviving; we're building a moat.

Next, new product launches and their contribution to growth. New product launches—defined as platforms introduced within the last 24 months—accounted for 42% of our total revenue in Q2, up from 35% in Q1 and 28% a year ago. That's $178 million in incremental revenue, representing a blistering 52% year-over-year growth for this cohort. This performance significantly outpaced our established portfolio, which grew a solid 18% YoY, underscoring the success of our 'innovation-first' strategy. Gross margins on these new launches came in at 68%, a 450-basis-point improvement sequentially, thanks to scale efficiencies in manufacturing and favorable ASP dynamics as we penetrate high-value accounts.

Our flagship launch, the NeoStent AI™—our next-generation drug-eluting coronary stent with embedded AI for real-time plaque characterization and deployment optimization—was the star performer. Cleared by the FDA in late Q4 last year under the Breakthrough Devices Program, NeoStent generated $92 million in Q2 sales, exceeding our initial guidance by 15%. Procedure volumes surged 61% quarter-over-quarter, driven by strong clinical data from our pivotal ORBIT-3 trial, which demonstrated a 37% reduction in target lesion failure rates at 12 months compared to predicate devices like Boston Scientific's Synergy XD. We've seen ASPs hold firm at around $2,450 per unit, bolstered by favorable CMS reimbursement under the new MS-DRG 286/287 codes for complex PCI procedures.

Complementing this, our CardioWear Pro™ remote patient monitoring patch—a wearable biosensor for continuous AFib detection and heart failure prognostication—ramped to $45 million in Q2 revenue, up 78% YoY. Integrated with our cloud-based MediCloud Analytics platform, it achieved a 92% patient compliance rate in real-world evidence from our 5,000-patient post-market study, far surpassing competitors like Medtronic's Reveal LINQ at 82%. This has unlocked recurring SaaS revenue streams, with our subscription attach rate hitting 65%—contributing $12 million in high-margin digital services alone.

Regionally, the U.S. remains our growth engine, representing 62% of new launch sales at $110 million, fueled by expanded hospital GPO contracts with Vizient and Premier, where we've gained 320 basis points of structural heart market share to 14.2%, per our internal tracking against Abbott's XIENCE platform. In Europe, post-CE Mark approval, NeoStent adoption accelerated 45% QoQ to €28 million, benefiting from the EU MDR transition and strong uptake in high-volume cath labs in Germany and France amid rising TAVR/PCI hybrid procedures. APAC is emerging as a hotspot, with $22 million in sales—led by Japan and China—where regulatory wins with PMDA and NMPA have positioned us ahead of the curve. We're forecasting APAC new launch growth to triple in FY24 as procedure volumes rebound post-COVID, tapping into a $15 billion TAM for AI-stents alone.

Strategically, these launches reflect our $450 million R&D investment over the past two years—9.2% of revenue—focused on three pillars: precision intervention, digital integration, and sustainability. For instance, NeoStent incorporates bioresorbable polymers reducing long-term metallic burden by 40%, aligning with ESG mandates from payers like UnitedHealth. Looking ahead, our Q3 pipeline includes the RoboAssist NX™ robotic navigation system for endovascular procedures, with first-in-human data showing 25% faster deployment times versus Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci in simulated models. We've also announced a co-development partnership with Siemens Healthineers for hybrid OR imaging integration, which we expect to add $200 million in addressable market by 2026.

In summary, new product launches aren't just contributing to growth—they're redefining it, with a projected 45-50% YoY trajectory for the full year, pushing consolidated guidance to $2.85-2.95 billion. This positions us to capture meaningful share in a $550 billion global medtech market growing at 5.8% CAGR through 2028, per Grand View Research.

Then, hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates. Adoption here refers to the rate at which we're securing new placements of our flagship FlexiBot robotic-assisted surgery platform—our minimally invasive system that's disrupting traditional laparoscopy and orthopedics—across hospital operating rooms and ASCs. This metric is particularly telling because it feeds directly into our annuity revenue stream from instruments, accessories, and service contracts, which now represent 68% of our total revenue, up from 62% a year ago.

Overall system adoption accelerated to 28% year-over-year, with 142 new FlexiBot placements globally—our strongest quarter since the post-COVID recovery. Breaking it down by channel: hospital adoption grew 18% YoY to 89 new systems, reflecting steady penetration in large IDNs like HCA Healthcare and Tenet, where we've now exceeded 15% market share in robotic-assisted general surgery. Utilization rates in these hospital installs averaged 22 procedures per system per month, up 12% sequentially, driven by our Tips and Tricks training modules that have boosted surgeon proficiency.

But the real story is in ASCs. Adoption here exploded 52% YoY to 53 new placements, representing 37% of our total installs this quarter, versus just 22% a year ago. This aligns with the broader industry shift toward outpatient procedures, where ASC volume for eligible cases like hernia repairs, cholecystectomies, and knee arthroscopies has surged 15-20% annually per SG-2 data. Our FlexiBot Nano model, with its compact footprint and single-use FlexiTips cartridges optimized for 45-minute procedures, is tailor-made for this. Average selling prices held firm at $1.85 million per Nano system, supporting a 14% gross margin expansion in our systems segment.

Regionally, the U.S. remains our powerhouse, accounting for 72% of placements with ASC adoption hitting 61% YoY growth—fueled by CMS reimbursement tailwinds under the 2024 OPPS final rule, which expanded pass-through status for robotic bundles. We've secured key wins at ASC chains like Surgical Care Affiliates and Regent Surgical Health, where procedure growth post-install averaged 35%. In Europe, adoption was more measured at 14% YoY overall, with hospitals at 20% but ASCs lagging at 8% due to persistent reimbursement silos in Germany and Italy—though our CE Mark renewal for the FlexiBot Prime with AI-driven tissue analytics has unlocked pilots at 12 new sites in the UK NHS. APAC showed breakout potential, up 45% to 16 placements, led by Japan where our partnership with Terumo has driven 28% hospital adoption amid the aging population boom; China ASCs, however, remain nascent at just 5 placements, constrained by NMPA approvals but poised for acceleration with our upcoming local manufacturing JV.

From a technical standpoint, our adoption surge ties directly to three initiatives. First, the FlexiBot 3.0 software upgrade, rolled out in June, integrates real-time haptic feedback and machine learning for predictive kinematics—reducing procedure times by 18% in beta trials and lifting conversion rates from demo to purchase to 78%. Second, our Value Analysis Committee playbook has shortened hospital sales cycles by 25% through bundled economics showing $2,200 cost savings per case versus legacy laparoscopy, akin to Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci playbook but with superior ergonomics for orthopedics. Third, in ASCs, our FlexiLease program—zero upfront capital with revenue share on procedures—has closed 40% of deals, mirroring Stryker's Mako success in joints but extended to soft tissue.

Strategically, we're laser-focused on capturing the $15 billion TAM for robotics in outpatient settings by 2028, per Grand View Research, as ASC procedure mix shifts from 25% to 40% of total volume. Competitors like Medtronic's Hugo and Johnson & Johnson's Ottava are ramping, but our 2.1-year payback period—versus their 2.7—gives us a clear edge, especially with 92% customer retention. Looking forward, we guide to 30-35% total adoption growth in FY24, with ASCs contributing over 40% of placements, which should drive 22-25% annuity revenue expansion.

Then, capital equipment versus consumables mix trends. This is a hallmark of the MedTech industry's razor-blade business model—capital sales like our advanced surgical robots, imaging systems, and navigation platforms serve as the "razor" to drive high-margin, annuity-like consumables revenue from procedures, implants, and disposables, akin to how Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci Xi systems fuel instrument and accessory utilization.

Total revenue came in at $2.55 billion, up 12% organically. Capital equipment represented 34% of the mix, or $867 million, down 400 basis points year-over-year from 38%. This reflects a deliberate moderation in capital placements as hospitals digest prior-year investments amid tighter capex budgets. Conversely, consumables hit a record 66% of the mix at $1.683 billion, up sequentially from 64% in Q2 and accelerating 18% organically year-over-year. Gross margins benefited accordingly, with consumables at 76% versus 52% for capital, driving overall blended margins to 68%, up 220 basis points.

Zooming out to the nine-month trailing period, capital at 36% of revenue, down from 41% in 9M'22, while consumables expanded to 64%, up from 59%. This shift contributed roughly 300 basis points to our recurring revenue growth, now at 72% of total sales—nearing our long-term target of 75%+. For context, peers like Stryker and Zimmer Biomet have hovered around 60-65% consumables in recent quarters, but our robotics and endovascular franchises are pulling us ahead.

Several factors underpinned this consumables acceleration. First, installed base expansion and utilization ramp: our active installed base grew 14% year-over-year to 4,200 systems across robotics like our PrecisionNav OR 2.0 platform and endovascular suites. Procedure volumes surged 22%, with utilization rates climbing to 285 procedures per system annually, up from 260. This was fueled by our next-gen single-use articulating instruments, which boast 20% higher precision and reduced cross-contamination risks versus reusables—critical post-COVID sterilization backlogs.

Second, ASP stability and mix within consumables: consumable ASPs held firm at $1,450 per procedure, flat sequentially despite inflationary pressures on raw materials like nitinol and PEEK. Premium mix shifted favorably, with high-acuity disposables like our drug-eluting stents and bioresorbable scaffolds in cardio now 45% of consumables revenue, up from 40%. This mirrors market dynamics where Abbott's XIENCE stents command premiums amid GLP-1 drug synergies boosting vascular procedures.

Third, capital moderation: capital sales grew a solid 8% to $867 million, led by 150 new PrecisionNav placements, but lagged consumables due to hospital consolidation and capex scrutiny. Bundle deals, where we pair systems with multi-year consumables commitments, closed 25% of deals, locking in $450 million in future annuity streams.

Regionally, U.S. consumables mix hit 70%, up 500 bps YoY, driven by ASC proliferation—ambulatory surgery centers now account for 28% of our ortho robotics procedures. Capital dipped to 30% as Vizient GPO contracts prioritized value-based bundles. Medicare reimbursement tailwinds for robotic-assisted hysterectomies added 10% to utilization. Europe saw strongest consumables growth at 25% organic, reaching 68% mix, thanks to MDR compliance for our single-use endoscopes. Emerging markets were capital-led at 45% mix, as China’s Healthy China 2030 initiatives spurred 60 new imaging system installs.

Strategically, we're doubling down through R&D pipeline investments of $450 million YTD in consumables innovation, including AI-enabled disposable trocars with haptic feedback and next-gen electrophysiology catheters. Commercial execution via our Consumables Assurance Program boosted attach rates to 1.8x per capital placement. Acquisitions like EndoDynamics added 200 bps to consumables mix.

Looking ahead, we see sustained tailwinds from aging demographics, minimally invasive surgery penetration, and payer shifts to value-based care. This mix trajectory enhances visibility—95% of FY'24 revenue now guided—and positions us for 14-16% organic growth and 25%+ EPS expansion.

Then, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains. We're pleased to highlight our disciplined approach to SG&A expense management, which delivered $48 million in year-over-year savings, or approximately 7% below our prior-year levels, while supporting 12% revenue growth. This translated to SG&A as a percentage of revenue improving 210 basis points to 25.4%, down from 27.5% in Q2 FY23. Sequentially, we saw a further 80 basis point decline from Q1 FY24, underscoring the sustainability of these gains amid persistent inflationary pressures and supply chain headwinds in the Medical Devices sector.

Selling expense optimization, 62% of total SG&A, came in at $312 million, a 5% reduction year-over-year, despite aggressive territory expansion in high-growth segments like structural heart and robotics-assisted surgery. Sales force right-sizing and productivity tools: we've optimized our U.S. field sales team by 4%, or 180 reps, through natural attrition and reallocating to high-potential accounts like Kaiser Permanente and HCA Healthcare. Leveraging Salesforce Einstein AI in our CRM, we've improved quota attainment by 15% via predictive analytics on surgeon adoption for products like our next-gen TAVR valves.

Digital selling and marketing shift: we've accelerated virtual engagements, cutting travel and trade show costs by 22%, or $18 million. Our VitalHub digital portal has driven 35% of U.S. case coverage through remote proctoring and VR simulations for robotic systems. In Europe, localized content boosted e-learning by 28%.

Regionally, U.S. SG&A leverage was 24.1%, aided by GPO renewals. EMEA improved to 27.8% despite neuromodulation investments. APAC kept expenses flat amid ortho growth.

G&A efficiency, 38% of total SG&A, totaled $198 million, down 10% YoY. Procurement and shared services centralization yielded $22 million in savings via SAP Ariba, negotiating 12-18% discounts. Automation with UiPath RPA bots automated 65% of invoice processing, reducing FTEs by 7%. Real estate rationalization subleased 25% of facilities, saving $8 million.

These gains are embedded in our MedTech Lean framework, targeting SG&A at 24-25% by FY25 end. We've unlocked $150 million in cumulative savings over 18 months, fueling 300 bps of adjusted operating margin expansion to 28.2%.

Finally, procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary. Procedure volume trends and market recovery have been key drivers of our 14% organic revenue growth this quarter. The medical devices industry has been navigating a multi-year recovery from COVID-19 disruptions, with elective procedures—particularly in structural heart, orthopedics, and neuromodulation—seeing a strong rebound. We're now entering sustained expansion, fueled by demographic tailwinds like aging populations, expanded indications for minimally invasive therapies, and accelerating adoption of robotics and AI-enabled devices.

Globally, our tracked procedure volumes grew 13% year-over-year in Q3, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit gains. This compares favorably to the broader market, where IQVIA estimates industry-wide elective procedure recovery at around 10-11% for the full year. Our outperformance stems from leadership in high-growth segments like TAVR and LAA closure, where we've gained share through our EvoValve platform and Watchman FLX Pro device.

By segment: Cardiovascular procedures up 18% YoY, with TAVR surging 25% driven by penetration into lower-risk patients. PCI grew 12%, LAA closure 22%. Orthopedics rebounded 11% YoY, knee replacements up 15% with robotic penetration at 28%. Neuromodulation and endoscopy rose 16% and 10%, respectively.

Regionally, U.S. up 16% YoY, Europe 8%, APAC 20% led by China’s 28% surge, Rest of World 14%.

We're capitalizing through $250 million R&D in AI-driven procedure planning, boosting efficiency by 15-20%. Our Vantage Outcomes database supports label expansions. M&A like NeuroStim Dynamics doubled our neuromodulation funnel.

We expect Q4 volumes to accelerate to 14-16% growth, with full-year organic at 13-15%. Tailwinds from 4 million annual U.S. TAVR-eligible patients through 2030 position us for 8-10% long-term procedure CAGR.

I will now turn the call over to Jennifer for a review of our financial results.

Jennifer Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered exceptional financial performance this quarter.
